title: Mitigating Demographic Disparities in Explanation-Human Alignment via Rationale Regularization
abstract: arXiv:2610.22586v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study explanation fairness in hate speech detection. High classification performance does not always mean that a model produces equally plausible explanations for different demographic groups. Using the HateXplain dataset, we introduce Plausibility-EFG, a metric that measures the largest difference in explanation plausibility across demographic groups by comparing model-generated token attributions with human-annotated rationales. We evaluate BERT, RoBERTa, and ADV-RoBERTa, an adversarially trained model, using Integrated Gradients and SHAP. Our results show that ADV-RoBERTa improves classification performance and alignment between explanations and human rationales while reducing explanation disparities across demographic groups. These improvements are observed with both attribution methods and remain consistent across training, validation, and test splits. translated_title: 通过理由正则化缓解解释与人类对齐中的人口群体差异
translated_abstract: 我们研究仇恨言论检测中的解释公平性。高分类性能并不总是意味着模型能够为不同人口群体产生同样合理的解释。使用HateXplain数据集，我们引入了Plausibility-EFG这一指标，通过比较模型生成的词元归因与人工标注的理由，来衡量不同人口群体之间解释合理性的最大差异。我们使用集成梯度和SHAP方法评估了BERT、RoBERTa以及对抗训练模型ADV-RoBERTa。结果表明，ADV-RoBERTa在提高分类性能和解释与人类理由之间对齐程度的同时，减少了不同人口群体之间的解释差异。这些改进在两种归因方法下均可观察到，并且在训练集、验证集和测试集上保持一致。我们还表明，仅减少预测层面的偏差并不能消除解释层面的差异。
tldr: 本文提出Plausibility-EFG指标来衡量仇恨言论检测模型在不同人口群体间解释合理性的差异，并证明采用理由正则化的对抗训练模型ADV-RoBERTa能在提升分类性能和解释与人类对齐的同时减少群体间的解释差异。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Plausibility-EFG, a metric measuring the largest difference in explanation plausibility across demographic groups in hate speech detection, and demonstrates that the rationale-regularized adversarially trained ADV-RoBERTa improves classification performance and explanation-human alignment while reducing explanation disparities across demographic groups.
